pyq_focus: Unit 5 se sabse zyada sawal 'book-author-year' type ke aate hain: Saussure 1916, Chomsky 1957 aur 1965, Austin 1962, Searle 1969, Grice 1975, Halliday ki books.
Match-the-following bahut common hai: method aur founder (Silent Way-Gattegno, Suggestopedia-Lozanov, TPR-Asher, CLL-Curran) aur concept aur linguist.
ELT aur SLA se lagbhag har paper mein kuch na kuch: Krashen ke 5 hypotheses, Selinker ka interlanguage, Corder ka error analysis, Prabhu ka TBLT, Hymes ka communicative competence.
Phonetics-phonology mein seedhe fact: RP ke 44 phonemes, place aur manner of articulation, voiced/voiceless, minimal pair, allophone, schwa.
Speech acts aur Grice ke maxims par 'which is NOT' aur assertion-reason sawal aate hain; Searle ki 5 categories ke examples pehchaanna seekho.
History of English mein chronology: 449, 1066, 1362, 1476, 1611, 1755, 1884 - dates ko line se yaad karo; Grimm's Law, Great Vowel Shift, Old Norse words.
Sociolinguistics: diglossia (Ferguson 1959), Labov 1966, Bernstein ke codes, Kachru ke circles, pidgin vs creole, code-switching vs code-mixing.
Testing: validity vs reliability, washback, formative vs summative, norm vs criterion-referenced, cloze - definitions par sawal.
Taiyari ka tarika: har topic ki 'naam - book - saal' table banao, roz 20 MCQ lagao, match wale pairs flash-card se revise karo aur galat sawalon ki list rakho.

easy.title: Ferdinand de Saussure and Structuralism
easy.story: Socho ek cricket team hai. Rules ki book sabke liye same hai - yeh langue hai. Har player jo maidan par asal mein khelta hai - woh parole hai. Saussure (Swiss, 1857-1913) ne kaha language ek system hai, jaise chess: har mohre ki value uski jagah se hoti hai. 'Gaay' shabd ki awaaz (signifier) aur dimaag mein gaay ki tasveer (signified) ka rishta arbitrary hai - English mein 'cow', Hindi mein 'gaay'. Unki Course in General Linguistics (1916) unke marne ke baad students ke notes se Bally aur Sechehaye ne chhaapi.
easy.trick: 'Saas-Bahu 1916': Langue = Saas ke rules (sabke liye), Parole = Bahu ka asli bolna. Editors 'Bali aur Sachi' = Bally aur Sechehaye. Synchronic = 'sync' = ek hi time, Diachronic = 'dia' = time ke aar-paar.

easy.title: Noam Chomsky and Generative Grammar
easy.story: Chhota bachcha bina sikhaaye naye-naye sentences bana leta hai - yeh kaise? Chomsky ne kaha dimaag mein ek built-in grammar machine hai: LAD aur Universal Grammar. Bhasha ka andar wala gyaan = competence, bolte waqt jo nikla = performance. 'Colorless green ideas sleep furiously' grammar mein sahi hai par matlab bekaar. 1957 mein Syntactic Structures aayi, 1959 mein unhone Skinner ke Verbal Behavior ki review mein behaviourism ko kaata, 1965 mein Aspects of the Theory of Syntax aayi.
easy.trick: '57-59-65': 57 mein Syntax, 59 mein Skinner ki pitaai, 65 mein Aspects. C-P = Competence pehle, Performance baad mein - jaise Chomsky ka C.

easy.title: M. A. K. Halliday and Functional Linguistics
easy.story: Halliday kehte the bhasha ek auzaar hai jo samaaj mein kaam karta hai - 'social semiotic'. Iske teen kaam (metafunctions): ideational (duniya ki baat batana), interpersonal (rishta banana), textual (baat ko jod kar text banana). Shaadi ke card mein Field = kya ho raha hai (shaadi), Tenor = kaun kisse baat kar raha hai (family se mehmaan), Mode = likha hua card. Halliday J. R. Firth ke shishya the. Ruqaiya Hasan ke saath Cohesion in English (1976) likhi.
easy.trick: Metafunctions 'I-I-T' = Ideational, Interpersonal, Textual - IIT jaisa! Register 'FTM' = Field, Tenor, Mode = 'Phir Tum Mile'.

easy.title: Speech Act Theory: Austin and Searle
easy.story: Pandit ji bolte hain 'Main tumhe pati-patni ghoshit karta hoon' - bolte hi shaadi ho gayi! Yeh performative hai: bolna hi karna hai. Austin (How to Do Things with Words, 1962) ne teen level diye: locution (bolna), illocution (iraada, jaise warning dena), perlocution (asar, jaise saamne wala darr gaya). Searle (Speech Acts, 1969) ne illocution ki 5 categories banayi. 'Namak pass karoge?' sawaal lagta hai par asal mein request hai - indirect speech act.
easy.trick: Searle ke 5 = 'Ram Didi Ko Ek Dosa' = Representatives, Directives, Commissives, Expressives, Declarations. Austin ke L-I-P = 'LIPs' se bolo, Iraada rakho, Parinaam dekho.

easy.title: Grice, Politeness and Pragmatics
easy.story: Dost se poocha 'Exam kaisa gaya?' aur woh bola 'Canteen ka samosa achha tha.' Seedha jawab nahi diya, par tum samajh gaye ki exam bura gaya - yeh implicature hai. Grice ne kaha baat-cheet mein hum cooperate karte hain (Cooperative Principle) aur 4 maxims maante hain: Quantity, Quality, Relation, Manner. Khule aam maxim todna = flouting. Brown aur Levinson ne 'face' yaani izzat bachane wali politeness samjhayi.
easy.trick: 4 maxims 'QQRM' = 'Kuch Kuch Rishta Mast' (Quantity, Quality, Relation, Manner). Logic and Conversation 1975 = '75 mein Grice ne gappe maare'.

easy.title: Phonetics
easy.story: Phonetics awaaz ka science hai: munh se awaaz kaise banti hai (articulatory), hawa mein kaise jaati hai (acoustic), kaan kaise sunta hai (auditory). 'Pa' bolo to dono honth milte hain - bilabial. 'Ka' bolo to jeebh ka pichhla hissa upar - velar. Gale par haath rakh kar 'zzz' bolo, kaanpan hoga - voiced; 'sss' mein nahi - voiceless. RP English mein 44 sounds hain: 24 consonants aur 20 vowels. Sabse common vowel schwa /ə/ hai, jaise 'about' ka pehla 'a'.
easy.trick: '44 = 24 + 20', aur 20 = 12 pure + 8 diphthong = '12 mahine, 8 din ki chhutti'. Daniel Jones = Cardinal Vowels - 'Cardinal' yaani bade padri, sab vowels ke guru.

easy.title: Phonology
easy.story: Phonology dekhta hai ki kaunsi awaaz matlab badalti hai. 'Pin' aur 'bin' mein sirf p aur b ka fark hai aur matlab badal gaya, toh /p/ aur /b/ alag phonemes hain (minimal pair). 'Pin' ka p hawa ke jhonke ke saath aata hai, 'spin' ka bina - par matlab same, toh yeh allophones hain. Jaise ek hi ladka ghar mein 'Golu' aur school mein 'Rahul' - insaan ek, roop do. 'Ten boys' jaldi bolo to 'tem boys' - assimilation.
easy.trick: Phoneme /slash/ mein, allophone [bracket] mein: 'Slash = asli family, Bracket = bhes badla roop'. Trubetzkoy 1939 = Prague ka 'Phono baba'.

easy.title: Morphology and Word Formation
easy.story: Shabd ko Lego blocks ki tarah todo: 'unhappiness' = un + happy + ness. Sabse chhota matlab wala block = morpheme. 'Book' akela khada ho sakta hai (free), '-s' akela nahi (bound). Smoke + fog = smog (blending), influenza se flu (clipping), editor se edit (back-formation). Google naam se 'to google' kriya ban gayi - yeh conversion hai.
easy.trick: 8 inflections: 'teen S, teen verb, do compare' = -s plural, -'s possessive, -s 3rd person; -ed, -en, -ing; -er, -est. Portmanteau = Lewis Carroll ka 'suitcase' jismein do matlab band.

easy.title: Syntax
easy.story: Syntax shabdon ko line mein lagane ka niyam hai, jaise train ke dibbe sahi kram mein. English mein order SVO hai: 'Ram eats mangoes'; Hindi mein SOV: 'Ram aam khaata hai'. Sentence ko chhote tukdon mein todna IC analysis hai (Bloomfield). Chomsky ne rule diya: S -> NP + VP. 'Visiting relatives can be boring' ke do matlab hain - structural ambiguity. 'The house that Jack built' jaisa sentence badhta hi jaata hai - recursion.
easy.trick: Quirk ke 7 patterns sab 'SV' se shuru: SV, SVO, SVC, SVA, SVOO, SVOC, SVOA = 'Sab Vidyarthi' ke saath extra dabbe. English SVO, Hindi SOV.

easy.title: Semantics
easy.story: Semantics matlab 'meaning ki padhai'. 'Rose' ek 'flower' hai - rose hyponym, flower superordinate, jaise 'aam' ek 'phal'. Garam-thanda gradable antonyms, zinda-murda complementary, kharidna-bechna converse. Bank (nadi ka kinara) aur bank (paise wala) homonym hain; head (sir) aur head of department polysemy hai. Subah ka taara aur shaam ka taara dono Venus hain - Frege ka sense vs reference.
easy.trick: Leech ke 7 meanings 'Chai Coffee Samosa Aur Roti Chhole Thali' = Conceptual, Connotative, Social, Affective, Reflected, Collocative, Thematic. Ogden-Richards 1923 = 'triangle wale dost'.

easy.title: Sociolinguistics
easy.story: Ghar par dadi se Haryanvi, college mein Hindi-English mix (Hinglish = code-mixing), office mein formal English - ek hi insaan, bhasha ke alag roop. Ferguson ne kaha kuch samaaj mein ek High (formal) aur ek Low (ghar wali) variety saath chalti hai - diglossia (1959). Labov ne New York ki dukaanon mein 'fourth floor' ka /r/ suna (1966). Kachru ke circles mein India Outer Circle mein hai. Sapir-Whorf kehte hain bhasha soch ko shape karti hai.
easy.trick: Kram yaad: 'Phir Lassi Bina Lassi nahi' = Ferguson 1959, Labov 1966, Bernstein 1971, Lakoff 1975. Pidgin = 'pehla, bina maa ka'; Creole = 'pidgin jo kisi ki maa-boli ban gaya'.

easy.title: History of the English Language
easy.story: English West Germanic bhasha hai, Indo-European parivaar ki beti - Sanskrit ki door ki cousin (William Jones ne 1786 mein Calcutta mein bataya). Lagbhag 449 AD mein Angles, Saxons aur Jutes Britain aaye - Old English shuru. Vikings ne 'they, sky, egg' jaise shabd diye; 1066 mein Normans aaye aur French ke dher shabd laaye. Caxton ki press (1476), King James Bible (1611), Johnson ki Dictionary (1755) - standard English bana. Great Vowel Shift mein lambi vowels munh mein upar khisak gayi.
easy.trick: Periods: Old 450, Middle 1100, Modern 1500 = 'saadhe chaar, gyarah, pandrah' sau. 'Grimm ne pater ko father banaya' = p > f.

easy.title: ELT Methods: GTM, Direct Method, ALM and Humanistic Methods
easy.story: Purane school mein grammar ka rule ratao aur Hindi mein translate karo - yeh Grammar Translation Method hai. Phir Berlitz jaise logon ne kaha mother tongue band, seedha English - Direct Method. World War II mein army ke liye ALM aaya: 'repeat after me', drill par drill, tote jaisa (behaviourism). Phir humanistic methods aaye: Silent Way (teacher chup, Gattegno), Suggestopedia (music ke saath relax, Lozanov), TPR (Asher - 'Stand up!' bolo aur khade ho jao), CLL (Curran - teacher counsellor).
easy.trick: 'Gattegno Goonga, Lozanov Lori (music), Asher Action, Curran Counsellor'. ALM = 'Army ka tota'.

easy.title: CLT, TBLT, Krashen and SLA Theories
easy.story: CLT kehta hai: grammar thoda galat ho to chalega, baat samjha do - fluency pehle. Dell Hymes ne 1972 mein 'communicative competence' shabd diya. Prabhu ne Bangalore mein tasks se padhaya, jaise train timetable dekh kar jawab nikalna (information gap). Krashen bole: bachcha apne level se thoda aage wala input samjhe (i+1) aur dar na ho (low affective filter), to bhasha khud aa jaati hai. Selinker ne learner ki beech wali bhasha ko 'interlanguage' kaha.
easy.trick: Krashen ke 5 = 'AMNIA' = Acquisition-learning, Monitor, Natural order, Input, Affective filter. i+1 = 'ek seedhi upar'.

easy.title: Language Testing and Evaluation
easy.story: Test ek tarazu hai. Tarazu sahi cheez tole - validity; har baar same wazan bataaye - reliability. Board exam ke darr se teacher sirf exam wala padhaye - washback. Saal ke beech ke chhote tests = formative, aakhri exam = summative. Cloze test mein har kuch shabd ke baad ek shabd gayab hota hai, bachcha bharta hai. Doosron se compare karna = norm-referenced; fixed cut-off se = criterion-referenced.
easy.trick: 'VRPW' = Validity, Reliability, Practicality, Washback = 'Vahi Ram Pass Wala'. Cloze = Taylor (1953) - 'darzi (tailor) ne khaali jagah silai'.

easy.title: Grammar and Usage (English in Use)
easy.story: Grammar do tarah ki: prescriptive (dadaji jaisi - 'aise bolo!', Lowth 1762) aur descriptive (reporter jaisi - log jaise bolte hain waisa likho). 'Neither the teacher nor the students were present' - verb paas wale subject ki baat maanta hai. 'No sooner... than' aur 'Hardly... when' pakki jodi hain. 'If I were rich' - second conditional mein 'were'. Indian English ki galtiyan: 'discuss about', 'return back', 'cousin brother'.
easy.trick: 'No sooner - THAN, Hardly - WHEN' = 'Nathan aur Hardwin do dost'. 'Lest' ke baad 'should', 'not' kabhi nahi.

Those elements that are similar to his native language will be simple for him, and those elements that are different will be difficult.
The making of errors is a device the learner uses in order to learn.
While without grammar very little can be conveyed, without vocabulary nothing can be conveyed.
We acquire by understanding input that contains structure a little beyond our current level of competence (i + 1).
quotes.source: Principles and Practice in Second Language Acquisition, 1982

quotes.quote: Language consists of grammaticalised lexis, not lexicalised grammar.

The zone of proximal development is the distance between the actual developmental level as determined by independent problem solving and the level of potential development as determined through problem solving under adult guidance or in collaboration with more capable peers.
Teaching should be subordinated to learning.
quotes.source: Principle of the Silent Way (Richards and Rodgers summary)

mcqs.q: Chomsky's distinction between a speaker's knowledge of language and its actual use is:
mcqs.exp: Aspects of the Theory of Syntax (1965) mein competence = knowledge, performance = use.

mcqs.q: The term 'communicative competence' was proposed by:
mcqs.exp: Dell Hymes ne Chomsky ke 'competence' ke jawab mein yeh concept diya (On Communicative Competence, 1972).

mcqs.q: Saussure described the linguistic sign as having two sides:
mcqs.exp: Sign = signifier (sound-image) + signified (concept); dono ka rishta arbitrary hai.

mcqs.q: Utterances like 'I name this ship Queen Elizabeth', which do something rather than describe, were called by Austin:
mcqs.exp: Austin ne constative (true/false statement) aur performative (action karne wala) mein farq kiya.

mcqs.q: In Searle's taxonomy, a promise is an example of a:
mcqs.exp: Commissive mein speaker khud ko future action se baandhta hai, jaise promise ya vow.

mcqs.q: Brown and Levinson's politeness theory is built on the concept of:
mcqs.exp: Politeness: Some Universals in Language Usage (1987) - positive face aur negative face.

mcqs.q: Words like 'here', 'now', 'I' and 'you', whose meaning depends on context, illustrate:
mcqs.exp: Deixis = context par nirbhar 'pointing' words: person, place, time deixis.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a voiceless labio-dental fricative?
mcqs.exp: /f/ voiceless labio-dental fricative hai; /v/ uska voiced pair hai.

mcqs.q: The vowel sound in the unstressed first syllable of 'about' is:
mcqs.exp: Schwa English ka sabse common weak vowel hai, unstressed syllables mein aata hai.

mcqs.q: The sound /ŋ/ as at the end of 'sing' is a:
mcqs.exp: /ŋ/ velar nasal hai; English mein yeh word ke shuru mein nahi aata.

mcqs.q: 'Ship' and 'sheep' differ in only one sound and form a:
mcqs.exp: Minimal pair do words jo ek hi phoneme se alag hon; yeh phonemes prove karta hai.

mcqs.q: The smallest meaningful unit of language is the:
mcqs.exp: Morpheme = smallest unit of meaning; phoneme = smallest unit of sound (meaning nahi).

mcqs.q: In the word 'unhappiness', 'un-' and '-ness' are:
mcqs.exp: Prefix aur suffix akele nahi aa sakte, isliye bound morphemes; 'happy' free morpheme hai.

mcqs.q: 'Laser' and 'NATO', pronounced as words, are examples of:
mcqs.exp: Initials se bana aur word ki tarah bola jaaye to acronym; BBC jaisa letter-by-letter initialism hai.

mcqs.q: 'Flu' from 'influenza' and 'lab' from 'laboratory' are examples of:
mcqs.exp: Lambe word ka hissa kaatna = clipping.

mcqs.q: Using 'google' as a verb ('Google it') from a noun is an example of:
mcqs.exp: Bina affix ke word class badalna = conversion (zero derivation).

mcqs.q: 'Rose' is a hyponym of 'flower'; 'flower' is therefore the:
mcqs.exp: Hyponymy mein upar wala general term superordinate/hypernym kehlata hai.

mcqs.q: A pidgin that becomes the native language of a community is called a:
mcqs.exp: Pidgin ka koi native speaker nahi hota; jab bachche ise mother tongue bana lein to creole.

mcqs.q: William Labov's 1966 study of the social stratification of English was carried out in:
mcqs.exp: The Social Stratification of English in New York City (1966); department store /r/ study.

mcqs.q: Old English is generally dated from about:
mcqs.exp: Old English c. 450-1100, Middle English c. 1100-1500, Early Modern c. 1500-1700.

mcqs.q: The first major Germanic sound change that distinguishes Germanic from other Indo-European languages is described by:
mcqs.exp: Grimm's Law (Jacob Grimm, 1822): p>f, t>θ, k>h, jaise Latin pater, English father.

mcqs.q: Chaucer wrote in which period of English?
mcqs.exp: Chaucer (d. 1400) Middle English ka sabse bada kavi; London dialect.

mcqs.q: Who published the first printed book in England, at Westminster?
mcqs.exp: Caxton ne 1476 mein Westminster mein press lagaya; isse spelling standard hone lagi.

mcqs.q: 'The Practical Study of Languages' (1899), a key text of the Reform Movement, was written by:
mcqs.exp: Henry Sweet ki The Practical Study of Languages (1899) Reform Movement ka mukhya granth hai.

mcqs.q: Which method forbids the use of the mother tongue and teaches through demonstration and oral interaction, often linked with Berlitz schools?
mcqs.exp: Direct Method: sirf target language, mother tongue nahi; Berlitz schools mein popular.

mcqs.q: Cuisenaire rods are associated with:
mcqs.exp: Caleb Gattegno ki Silent Way mein coloured rods aur Fidel charts use hote hain.

mcqs.q: Krashen's 'i + 1' refers to:
mcqs.exp: Input Hypothesis: learner ke current level (i) se thoda upar (i+1) wala comprehensible input.

mcqs.q: Lev Vygotsky's 'Zone of Proximal Development' refers to:
options: What a learner can do with help but not yet alone
The gap between L1 and L2
mcqs.exp: ZPD = jo bachcha akele nahi par madad (scaffolding) se kar sake.

mcqs.q: The Critical Period Hypothesis for language acquisition is chiefly associated with:
mcqs.exp: Lenneberg, Biological Foundations of Language (1967).

mcqs.q: Skinner's behaviourist account of language, 'Verbal Behavior' (1957), was famously reviewed and attacked by:
mcqs.exp: Chomsky ka review (1959) behaviourism ke against turning point maana jaata hai.

mcqs.q: The Contrastive Analysis Hypothesis, comparing L1 and L2 to predict difficulty, is associated with:
mcqs.exp: Robert Lado, Linguistics Across Cultures (1957).

mcqs.q: A test that measures what it is intended to measure is said to have:
mcqs.exp: Validity = sahi cheez naapna; reliability = baar baar same result dena.

mcqs.q: A test in which every nth word of a passage is deleted for the learner to restore is a:
mcqs.exp: Cloze (W. L. Taylor, 1953) mein har nth word delete hota hai.

mcqs.q: A test that compares a candidate's performance with that of other candidates is:
mcqs.exp: Norm-referenced = doosron se tulna (rank); criterion-referenced = fixed standard se tulna.

mcqs.q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:
options: He is more senior than me.
mcqs.exp: Latin-origin comparatives (senior, junior, superior, prefer) ke saath 'to' aata hai, 'than' nahi.

mcqs.q: Choose the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement:
options: Each of the boys has done his homework.
Each of the boys have done their homework.
Each of the boys have done his homework.
Each of the boy has done his homework.
mcqs.exp: 'Each of + plural noun' ke baad singular verb aata hai.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct form: 'If I ___ you, I would accept the offer.'
mcqs.exp: Unreal/hypothetical condition mein formal English 'If I were' (subjunctive) leti hai.

mcqs.q: Identify the correct sentence:
options: I have been living here since 2015.
mcqs.exp: Stative verbs (know, have=possess, belong) continuous mein nahi aate; 'since' ke saath perfect continuous sahi.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct article usage:
mcqs.exp: Article sound se tay hota hai: 'hour' silent h (an), 'university/one' consonant sound (a).

mcqs.q: In 'The man who came yesterday is my uncle', the clause 'who came yesterday' is a:
mcqs.exp: 'who' noun 'man' ko describe karta hai, isliye relative/adjective clause.

mcqs.q: Match the books with their authors: (a) Language (1921) (b) Language (1933) (c) Cours de linguistique generale (1916) (d) Course in Modern Linguistics (1958) | (i) Saussure (ii) Hockett (iii) Sapir (iv) Bloomfield
mcqs.exp: Sapir - Language (1921); Bloomfield - Language (1933); Hockett - A Course in Modern Linguistics (1958).

mcqs.q: Match the terms with the linguists who introduced them: (a) Interlanguage (b) Diglossia (c) Affective filter (d) Restricted code | (i) Krashen (ii) Bernstein (iii) Selinker (iv) Ferguson
mcqs.exp: Selinker 1972, Ferguson 1959, Krashen, Bernstein.

mcqs.q: Match the place of articulation with the sound: (a) Bilabial (b) Dental (c) Velar (d) Glottal | (i) /k/ (ii) /h/ (iii) /m/ (iv) /θ/
mcqs.exp: /m/ bilabial, /θ/ dental, /k/ velar, /h/ glottal.

mcqs.q: Match the word-formation process with the example: (a) Blending (b) Back-formation (c) Compounding (d) Borrowing | (i) babysit from babysitter (ii) motel (iii) bungalow (iv) blackboard
mcqs.exp: motel = motor+hotel (blend); babysit (back-formation); blackboard (compound); bungalow Hindi/Bengali se borrowing.

mcqs.q: Match Searle's speech act categories with examples: (a) Representative (b) Directive (c) Expressive (d) Declaration | (i) 'I apologise' (ii) 'I now pronounce you husband and wife' (iii) 'The earth is round' (iv) 'Please close the door'
mcqs.exp: Statement = representative; request = directive; apology = expressive; pronouncing marriage = declaration.

mcqs.q: Match Grice's maxims with what they demand: (a) Quantity (b) Quality (c) Relation (d) Manner | (i) Be relevant (ii) Be clear and avoid ambiguity (iii) Be as informative as required (iv) Do not say what you believe false
mcqs.exp: Quantity = jitna zaroori; Quality = sach; Relation = relevant; Manner = clear.

mcqs.q: Match the method with its key feature: (a) Audio-Lingual Method (b) Suggestopedia (c) Total Physical Response (d) Community Language Learning | (i) Counselling and the learner as client (ii) Pattern drills and habit formation (iii) Baroque music and relaxation (iv) Responding to commands with actions
mcqs.exp: ALM drills; Lozanov music; Asher commands; Curran counselling.

mcqs.q: Match the book with its author: (a) How to Do Things with Words (b) Speech Acts (c) Principles of Pragmatics (d) Cohesion in English | (i) Leech (ii) Halliday and Hasan (iii) Austin (iv) Searle
mcqs.exp: Austin 1962, Searle 1969, Leech 1983, Halliday and Hasan 1976.

mcqs.q: Match the language with the English loanword it gave: (a) French (b) Old Norse (c) Hindi (d) Arabic | (i) shampoo (ii) algebra (iii) beef (iv) sky
mcqs.exp: beef (French boeuf), sky (Norse), shampoo (Hindi champo), algebra (Arabic al-jabr).

mcqs.q: Match the type of test with its purpose: (a) Placement test (b) Diagnostic test (c) Achievement test (d) Proficiency test | (i) Measures general ability regardless of any course (ii) Identifies specific strengths and weaknesses (iii) Puts learners in the right level (iv) Measures what was learnt in a course
mcqs.exp: Placement = level; diagnostic = kamzori; achievement = course; proficiency = general ability (e.g. IELTS).

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): The relationship between the signifier and the signified is arbitrary. Reason (R): There is no natural connection between the sound sequence 'tree' and the concept of a tree.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: Saussure: arbitrariness ka matlab hi yahi hai ki sound aur concept ka koi natural link nahi; R, A ko explain karta hai.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): Allophones of a phoneme can change the meaning of a word. Reason (R): Allophones occur in complementary distribution or free variation.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: Allophones meaning nahi badalte, isliye A false; R sahi hai.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): English spelling is often not phonetic. Reason (R): The Great Vowel Shift changed the pronunciation of long vowels after spelling had begun to be fixed by printing.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: Printing (1476 ke baad) se spelling jam gayi aur GVS se pronunciation badal gaya; isiliye mismatch.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): English has a large number of French-derived words in the fields of law, government and food. Reason (R): English belongs to the Germanic branch of the Indo-European family.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: Dono sach hain, par Germanic hona French words ki wajah nahi; wajah Norman Conquest (1066) hai.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): The Audio-Lingual Method stresses drills and habit formation. Reason (R): It was based on Chomsky's transformational-generative grammar.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: ALM behaviourism aur structural linguistics par based tha, Chomsky par nahi; R false.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): In a creole there are native speakers. Reason (R): A pidgin has no native speakers.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: Dono sach hain, par pidgin mein native speaker na hona creole mein native speaker hone ki wajah nahi batata.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): Grice's maxims are rules that speakers always obey. Reason (R): Conversational implicature often arises when a speaker flouts a maxim.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: Maxims hamesha follow nahi hote, isliye A false; flouting se implicature banta hai, R true.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): A test can be reliable without being valid. Reason (R): Reliability concerns consistency of results, while validity concerns whether the test measures what it should.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: Consistent result dena (reliability) sahi cheez naapne (validity) ki guarantee nahi; R hi A ko explain karta hai.

mcqs.q: Arrange in chronological order: (i) Searle, Speech Acts (ii) Brown and Levinson, Politeness (iii) Austin, How to Do Things with Words (iv) Grice, Logic and Conversation
mcqs.exp: Austin 1962, Searle 1969, Grice 1975, Brown and Levinson 1987.

mcqs.q: Arrange Chomsky's works in chronological order: (i) Aspects of the Theory of Syntax (ii) The Minimalist Program (iii) Syntactic Structures (iv) Lectures on Government and Binding
Arrange these language teaching methods in the order in which they emerged: (i) Communicative Language Teaching (ii) Direct Method (iii) Grammar-Translation Method (iv) Audio-Lingual Method
mcqs.exp: GTM 19th century, Direct Method late 19th, ALM 1950s, CLT 1970s.

mcqs.q: Arrange in chronological order: (i) Caxton's printing press at Westminster (ii) Statute of Pleading (iii) Authorised (King James) Version of the Bible (iv) Norman Conquest
Arrange in chronological order: (i) Halliday, Language as Social Semiotic (ii) Bloomfield, Language (iii) Chomsky, Syntactic Structures (iv) Saussure, Course in General Linguistics

Arrange these SLA works in chronological order: (i) Selinker, Interlanguage (ii) Lado, Linguistics Across Cultures (iii) Krashen, Principles and Practice in Second Language Acquisition (iv) Corder, The Significance of Learners' Errors

Arrange these dictionaries in chronological order: (i) Johnson's Dictionary of the English Language (ii) Cawdrey's A Table Alphabeticall (iii) First part of the Oxford English Dictionary (A New English Dictionary) (iv) Webster's An American Dictionary of the English Language
Which of the following statements is correct?
mcqs.exp: /z/ voiced hai, /ʃ/ palato-alveolar fricative, /w/ labial-velar approximant; sirf /l/ wala statement sahi.

mcqs.q: Identify the correct statement about M. A. K. Halliday:
options: He proposed the theory of Universal Grammar.
His textual metafunction deals with social relations between speakers.
mcqs.exp: Halliday = Systemic Functional Linguistics; social relations interpersonal metafunction hai; UG aur Syntactic Structures Chomsky ke.

mcqs.q: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: The Norman Conquest of 1066 brought a large number of French words into English.
Old Norse words entered English mainly through the Normans.
mcqs.exp: Norse words Viking/Danish settlers se aaye; Shakespeare Early Modern English; Johnson 1755.

mcqs.q: Identify the correct statement about assessment:
options: Summative assessment is carried out continuously to guide day-to-day teaching.
Formative assessment takes place during a course to give feedback and improve learning.
A norm-referenced test measures performance against a fixed criterion.
mcqs.exp: Formative = course ke dauran feedback; summative = end mein; washback positive bhi ho sakta hai.

mcqs.q: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct?
options: One of my friend live in Delhi.
He did not went to school.
The news are very good today.
mcqs.exp: Mathematics aur news dikhne mein plural par singular verb lete hain; one of + plural noun, did + base verb.
